Ibn al-Mubārak, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Aḥmad and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from al-Shaʿbī, who said: Whenever the Hour was mentioned in the presence of Jesus son of Mary, he would cry out and say: It is not fitting for the son of Mary that the Hour be mentioned in his presence and he keep silent.

Aḥmad and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Mujāhid, who said: Jesus used to wear hair-cloth and eat of the trees; he did not store up today for tomorrow, and he spent the night wherever night sheltered him; he had no child to die, and no house to fall into ruin.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from al-Ḥasan: Jesus is the head of the renunciants on the Day of Resurrection, and those who flee with their religion will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with Jesus son of Mary. And Iblīs passed by Jesus one day while he was using a stone as a pillow and had found the pleasure of sleep, and Iblīs said to him: O Jesus, do you not claim that you want nothing of the goods of this world? Yet this stone is of the goods of this world. So Jesus got up, took the stone and threw it away, and said: This is yours, together with the world.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Kaʿb that Jesus used to eat barley, walk on his feet and not ride beasts; he did not live in houses, nor light a lamp, nor wear cotton, nor touch women; he never touched perfume, never mixed his drink with anything at all, nor cooled it; he never oiled his head, and no wash ever came near his head or his beard; he never put anything between the ground and his skin except his garment; he never concerned himself about a morning meal or about an evening meal, and he desired nothing of the desires of this world. He used to sit with the weak, the chronically ill and the poor. When food was brought near to him upon something, he would set it down on the ground; he never ate any condiment with his food; he contented himself from this world with little sustenance, and he would say: This is a great deal for one who will die and be called to account for it.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from al-Ḥasan, who said: It reached me that it was said to Jesus son of Mary: Marry. He said: And what would I do with marriage? They said: She would bear you children. He said: Children, if they live they cause trial, and if they die they cause grief.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, recorded from Ashʿath ibn Isḥāq, who said: It was said to Jesus: If only you would take a house. He said: The worn-out remnants of those who were before us suffice us.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and al-Bayhaqī recorded from Maysarah, who said: It was said to Jesus: Will you not build yourself a house? He said: I shall not leave behind me anything of this world by which I would be remembered.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Abū Sulaymān, who said: While Jesus was walking on a summer's day, afflicted by the heat, the sun and thirst, he sat down in the shade of a tent. The owner of the tent came out to him and said: O servant of God, get up out of our shade. So Jesus got up and sat in the sun, and said: It is not you who made me get up; the One who made me get up is He who did not wish that I should obtain anything of this world.

Aḥmad recorded from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, who said: Jesus and John (peace be upon them both) would come to a village, and Jesus would ask after the worst of its people while John would ask after the best of its people. He said to him: Why do you lodge with the worst of people? He said: I am only a physician, treating the sick.

Aḥmad recorded from Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī, who said: It reached me that among the wisdom of Jesus son of Mary is: You work for this world, while you are provided for in it without work; and you do not work for the Hereafter, while you are not provided for in it except by work. Woe to you, evil scholars! You take the wage and waste the work! You are about to go out of this world into the darkness of the grave and its narrowness. God, Mighty and Majestic, forbids you acts of disobedience just as He commanded you fasting and prayer. How can he be among the people of knowledge whose world is dearer to him than his Hereafter, and who is more eager in desire for this world? How can he be among the people of knowledge whose journey is towards his Hereafter while he faces towards his world, and what harms him is more appetising to him than what benefits him? How can he be among the people of knowledge who is discontented and despises his station, while he knows that this is from God's knowledge and His power? How can he be among the people of knowledge who accuses God, Exalted, in His decree, so that he is not content with anything that befalls him? How can he be among the people of knowledge who seeks speech to talk, and does not seek it to act upon it?

Aḥmad recorded from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his elders, that Jesus (peace be upon him) passed by the pass of Afīq{{fn:ʿAqabat Afīq: a mountain pass east of the Sea of Galilee, on the road to Damascus.}} with one of his disciples, when a man confronted them and barred their way, saying: I shall not let the two of you pass until I have slapped each one of you a slap. They tried to put him off, but he would accept nothing else. So Jesus said: As for my cheek, slap it. He slapped it and let him go, and he said to the disciple: I shall not let you pass until I slap you. He resisted him; and when Jesus saw that, he gave him his other cheek, and he slapped it and let the two of them go. Then Jesus (peace be upon him) said: O God, if this is pleasing to You, then convey me to Your good pleasure; and if this is displeasing to You, then You are the most entitled to pardon.

ʿAbd Allāh his son recorded from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, who said: While Jesus (peace be upon him) was sitting with his companions a woman passed by him, and one of them looked at her. One of his companions said to him: You have committed adultery. Jesus said to him: What do you think, if you were fasting and passed by roast meat and smelt it, would you have broken your fast? He said: No.

Aḥmad recorded from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: Jesus said: I do not enter a village whose people wish to expel me from it but that they expel me, meaning: I have nothing in it. He said: And Jesus used to make himself sandals of the bark of trees, and make their thongs of palm fibre.
Aḥmad recorded from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: The Messiah said: Not as I want, but as You want; and not as I will, but as You will.
Aḥmad recorded from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: It reached me that there was no word that could be said of Jesus more beloved to him than that it be said: This poor wretch.
His son recorded from Ibn Ḥalbas, who said: Jesus said: Satan is with this world, his cunning is with wealth, his adornment is with passion, and his consummation is with the desires.

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad recorded from Jaʿfar ibn Burqān, who said: Jesus used to say: O God, I have come to morning unable to ward off what I dislike, and not possessing the benefit of what I hope for; the matter has come to be in the hand of another than me, and I have become pledged by my works. There is no poor man poorer than I. So do not let my enemy gloat over me, nor let my friend be grieved by me; do not make my affliction be in my religion, and do not give power over me to one who will not have mercy on me.

Aḥmad recorded from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: In the books of the disciples: When you are led along the path of affliction, know that you are being led along the path of the prophets and the righteous; and when you are led along the path of the people of ease, know that you are being led along other than their path, and are being turned aside from their way.

Aḥmad recorded from Mālik ibn Dīnār, who said: Jesus said: I send you only like rams, to gather up the lambs of the Children of Israel; so do not be like ravening wolves that snatch away the people; keep to the lambs. What is it with you, that you come wearing garments of hair while your hearts are the hearts of swine? Wear the garments of kings, and soften your hearts with fear. And Jesus said: O son of Adam, do the works of righteousness until your work reaches the clouds of heaven, and do them out of love for God; whatever you have done avails nothing of that in His sight without it. And Jesus said to the disciples: Iblīs wants to make you stingy, so do not fall into his stinginess.

Aḥmad recorded from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣanʿānī, who said: It reached us that Jesus (peace be upon him) said: O company of disciples, pray to God to lighten for me this agony, meaning death. Then Jesus said: I have feared death with such a fear that my fear of death has set me face to face with death.

Aḥmad recorded from Wahb ibn Munabbih that Jesus (peace be upon him) was standing at a grave with the disciples, while the owner of the grave was being lowered into it, and they spoke of the darkness of the grave, its desolation and its narrowness. Jesus said: You have already been in what is narrower than it: in the wombs of your mothers. When God loves to make room, He makes room.

Aḥmad recorded from Wahb, who said: The Messiah (peace be upon him) said: Remember God much, praise Him and hallow Him, and obey Him; for it is enough for one of you, by way of supplication, when God, Blessed and Exalted, is pleased with him, that he say: O God, forgive me my sin, set right for me my livelihood, and preserve me from what is hateful, O my God.

Aḥmad recorded from Abū al-Jald that Jesus (peace be upon him) said to the disciples: Truly I say to you: it is neither this world you want nor the Hereafter. They said: O Messenger of God, explain this to us, for we used to think that we wanted one of the two. He said: Had you wanted this world you would have obeyed the Lord of this world, in whose hand are the keys of its treasuries, and He would have given it to you; and had you wanted the Hereafter you would have obeyed the Lord of the Hereafter, who owns it, and He would have given it to you. But it is neither this you want, nor that.

Aḥmad recorded from Abū ʿUbaydah that the disciples said to Jesus: What shall we eat? He said: You shall eat barley bread and the herbs of the open country. They said: Then what shall we drink? He said: You shall drink plain water. They said: Then what shall we lay our heads upon? He said: Lay your heads upon the ground. They said: We see you commanding us nothing by way of livelihood but what is hard. He said: And by this you will be saved. You will not enter the kingdom of the heavens until one of you does this while he still has an appetite for it. They said: And how can that be? He said: Have you not seen that when a man is hungry, how beloved to him is a crust, even if it is of barley! And if he is thirsty, how beloved to him is water, even if it is plain! And when he has stood long, how beloved to him is to lay his head upon the ground.

Aḥmad recorded from ʿAṭāʾ that it reached him that Jesus (peace be upon him) said: Hope for no more than a bare sufficiency; be wakeful in the hours of heedlessness; judge with the subtlety of discernment; and do not be like a saddle-cloth cast aside while you are alive and breathing.

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad recorded from Abū Hurayrah, who said: Jesus (peace be upon him) used to say: O company of disciples, take your houses as way-stations, take the mosques as dwellings, eat of the herbs of the open country, and go out of this world in peace.
Aḥmad recorded from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī that Jesus (peace be upon him) said: Lay up your treasures in heaven, for a man's heart is with his treasure.

Ibn Abī Shaybah recorded from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd al-Juʿfī, who said: Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: My house is the mosque, my perfume is water, my condiment is hunger, my inner garment is fear, my mount is my two legs, my fireside in winter is the places where the sun rises, my lamp by night is the moon, and my companions are the chronically ill and the poor; I pass the evening with nothing, and I come to morning with nothing, and I am well. So who is richer than I?

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, who said: Jesus said: This world has been laid flat for you, and you sit upon its back; none will contend with you for it except kings and women. As for the kings, do not contend with them for this world, for they will never trouble you so long as you leave them and their world alone; and as for women, guard yourselves against them with fasting and prayer.
Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Sufyān al-Thawrī, who said: The Messiah said: This world is sought only to do good; but leaving it is better.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Shuʿayb ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: Jesus son of Mary said: By God, this world has not settled in the heart of a servant but that his heart has become bound by it to three things: a preoccupation whose toil never ceases, a poverty whose sufficiency is never reached, and a hope whose end is never attained. This world is both seeker and sought: the seeker of the Hereafter is sought by this world until he has received his provision from it in full, and the seeker of this world is sought by the Hereafter until death comes and seizes him by the neck.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Yazīd ibn Maysarah, who said: Jesus son of Mary said: As you humble yourselves, so you will be raised; as you show mercy, so you will be shown mercy; and as you fulfil the needs of people, so God will fulfil your needs.

Aḥmad and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from al-Shaʿbī, who said: Jesus son of Mary said: Beneficence is not that you do good to one who has done good to you, that is recompense; beneficence is only that you do good to one who has done evil to you.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Ibn al-Mubārak, who said: It reached me that Jesus son of Mary passed by a people who reviled him, and he spoke good; and he passed by others who reviled him and did more, and he gave them more good. A man among the disciples said: The more they increase in evil to you, the more you increase in good to them, as though you were inciting them against yourself! Jesus said: Every person gives what he has.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded from Mālik ibn Anas, who said: A pig passed by Jesus son of Mary, and he said: Pass in peace. It was said to him: O Spirit of God, do you say this to this pig? He said: I dislike accustoming my tongue to evil.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded from Sufyān, who said: They said to Jesus son of Mary: Direct us to a deed by which we may enter Paradise. He said: Never speak. They said: We cannot do that. He said: Then speak nothing but good.

Al-Kharāʾiṭī recorded from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, who said: Jesus son of Mary said: Take the truth from the people of falsehood, and do not take falsehood from the people of truth. Be critics of speech, so that counterfeits do not pass current upon you.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Zuhd, recorded from Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī, who said: Jesus son of Mary said: O company of disciples, be content with the meanness of this world together with the soundness of religion, just as the people of this world are content with the meanness of religion together with the soundness of this world.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Mālik ibn Dīnār, who said: Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: Eating barley with ashes, and sleeping on dunghills with the dogs, is little indeed in the quest for Paradise.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: Jesus son of Mary used to say: No servant can bear to have two lords: if he pleases one of them he angers the other, and if he angers one of them he pleases the other. Likewise no servant can bear to be a servant of this world while doing the work of the Hereafter. Do not be anxious about what you will eat or what you will drink, for God has not created a soul greater than its provision, nor a body greater than its clothing; so take heed.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from al-Maqburī that it reached him that Jesus son of Mary used to say: O son of Adam, when you do a good deed, forget about it, for it is with One who will not let it be lost; and when you do an evil deed, set it before your eyes.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl that Jesus son of Mary used to say: Whoever thinks that greed increases his provision, let him add to his height, or to his breadth, or to the number of his buildings, or let him change his colour. Indeed, God created the creation, and the creation proceeded according to what He created; then He apportioned provision, and provision proceeded according to what He apportioned. This world gives no one anything that is not his, nor does it withhold from anyone anything that is his. So hold fast to the worship of your Lord, for you were created for it.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from ʿImrān ibn Sulaymān, who said: It reached me that Jesus said to his companions: If you are my brothers and my companions, then accustom yourselves to enmity and hatred from people.
Aḥmad and al-Bayhaqī recorded from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ẓabyān, who said: The Messiah said: Whoever learns, acts and teaches, that one is called great in the kingdom of heaven.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Jesus son of Mary stood up among the Children of Israel and said: O company of disciples, do not speak wisdom to those who are not its people, lest you wrong it; and do not withhold it from its people, lest you wrong them. Affairs are three: a matter whose right guidance is clear, so follow it; a matter whose error is clear to you, so avoid it; and a matter about which you differ, so refer the knowledge of it to God, Exalted."

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Mulāʾī, who said: Jesus son of Mary said: If you withhold wisdom from its people you act in ignorance, and if you grant it to those who are not its people you act in ignorance. Be like the physician who treats: if he sees a place for the remedy he applies it, and otherwise he holds back.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Zuhd, and Ibn ʿAsākir, recorded from ʿIkrimah, who said: Jesus son of Mary said to the disciples: O company of disciples, do not cast pearls before swine, for the swine does nothing with the pearl; and do not give wisdom to one who does not want it, for wisdom is better than pearls, and one who does not want it is worse than the swine.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Jesus said: O evil scholars, you have sat at the gates of Paradise; you neither enter it yourselves nor let the poor enter it. The worst of people with God is a scholar who seeks this world by means of his knowledge.

Ibn Abī Shaybah recorded from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, who said: Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: The likeness of the soul's whispering of sin is the likeness of smoke in a house: if it does not burn it, it makes its smell foul and changes its colour.
### His words, Exalted: and the Torah and the Gospel (3:48)
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Qatādah, who said: Jesus used to recite the Torah and the Gospel.
### His words, Exalted: that I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird (3:49)

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Ibn Isḥāq, that Jesus sat one day with some boys from the school, and he took clay, then said: "Shall I make for you out of this clay a bird?" They said: "And can you do that?" He said: "Yes, by the permission of my Lord." Then he shaped it, until, when he had made it into the form of a bird, he breathed into it, then said: "Be a bird, by the permission of God." And it went out flying from between his two palms. The boys went out with this deed of his and mentioned it to their teacher, and they spread it abroad among the people.
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, that Jesus said: "Which of the birds is the hardest in its creation?" They said: "The bat; for it is nothing but flesh." So he made it.
Abū al-Shaykh recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Jesus created only one bird, and it was the bat.
### His words, Exalted: and I heal the one born blind and the leper (3:49)
Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The akmah is the one who is born blind.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The akmah is the blind man whose eye is smoothed over.{{fn:That is, one whose eye socket is flat and sealed, with no eye visible.}}

Abū ʿUbayd, al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn al-Anbārī in the Kitāb al-Aḍdād recorded, from Mujāhid, who said: The akmah is the one who sees by day and does not see by night.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn al-Anbārī recorded, from ʿIkrimah, who said: The akmah is the bleary-eyed (aʿmash).

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: The supplication of Jesus with which he used to pray for the sick, the chronically ill, the blind, the mad and others was: "O God, You are the God of whoever is in heaven and the God of whoever is on earth; there is no god in them besides You. You are the Compeller of whoever is in heaven and the Compeller of whoever is on earth; there is no compeller in them besides You. You are the King of whoever is in heaven and the King of whoever is on earth; there is no king in them besides You. Your power on earth is like Your power in heaven, and Your authority on earth is like Your authority in heaven. I ask You by Your noble Name, Your radiant Face and Your eternal dominion; truly You have power over all things." Wahb said: This is for the one seized with terror and for the madman: it is recited over him and written out for him, and he is given its water to drink, God willing.

Ibn Jarīr recorded, by another route, from Wahb, who said: When Jesus reached twelve years of age, God revealed to his mother, while she was in the land of Egypt, for she had fled from her people to the land of Egypt when she gave birth to him: "Go up with him to Syria." She did so, and she remained in Syria until he was thirty years old. His prophethood lasted three years, and then God raised him to Himself. Wahb claimed that sometimes there would gather around Jesus, in a single assembly, fifty thousand of the sick: whoever of them was able to reach him reached him, and whoever of them was not able to do so, Jesus would come to him, walking to him. And he treated them only by supplication to God, Exalted.
### His words, Exalted: and I give life to the dead by the permission of God (3:49)

Al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, by way of Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, from a man, that Jesus son of Mary, when he wished to give life to the dead, would pray two units of prayer (rakʿahs), reciting in the first Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (67:1), and in the second The sending down (32:2) of "al-Sajdah". When he had finished, he would praise God and extol Him, then call upon Him by seven names: O Eternal (Qadīm), O Living (Ḥayy), O Everlasting (Dāʾim), O Single (Fard), O Odd (Witr), O One (Aḥad), O Self-Sufficient (Ṣamad). Al-Bayhaqī said: This is not strong.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded it, by way of Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif, from Abū Bishr, from Abū al-Hudhayl, with its wording, and added at its end: And when hardship befell him, he would call upon Him by seven other names: O Living, O Self-Subsisting (Qayyūm), O God, O Most Merciful (Raḥmān), O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, O Light of the heavens and the earth and what is between them and Lord of the Mighty Throne, O my Lord.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded in Kitāb Man ʿāsha baʿd al-mawt (The Book of Those Who Lived after Death), from Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: The Children of Israel asked Jesus, saying: "Shem son of Noah is buried near here, so pray to God to raise him up for us." The prophet of God called out to him, but saw nothing; and he called out, but saw nothing. They said: "He was indeed buried near here." The prophet of God called out, and he came forth, grey-haired. They said: "He died while he was a young man, so what is this whiteness?" He said: "I thought it was the Cry,{{fn:The Cry (al-ṣayḥah) is the blast of the Trumpet that raises the dead on the Day of Resurrection.}} and I was terrified."

Isḥāq ibn Bishr and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, by several routes, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Jews used to gather around Jesus and mock him, saying to him: "O Jesus, what did so-and-so eat last night, and what did he store away in his house for tomorrow?" He would tell them, and they would scoff at him. This went on at length between him and them, and Jesus had no settled abode and no known place; he was only a wanderer in the land. One day he passed by a woman sitting by a grave, weeping. He asked her, and she said: "A daughter of mine has died, and I had no child other than her." So Jesus prayed two rakʿahs, then called out: "O so-and-so, rise by the permission of the Most Merciful, and come forth!" The grave stirred. Then he called a second time, and the grave split open. Then he called a third time, and she came out, shaking the dust from her head. She said: "O mother, what moved you to make me taste the agony of death twice? O mother, be patient and seek your reward with God, for I have no need of this world. O Spirit of God, ask my Lord to return me to the Hereafter and to make the agonies of death easy for me." So he prayed to his Lord, and He took her to Himself, and the earth settled level over her. That reached the Jews, and they increased in anger against him. Now there was a king of theirs in a certain region, in a city called Nisibis,{{fn:Naṣībīn, a city in upper Mesopotamia, today Nusaybin in south-eastern Turkey.}} a tyrannical and insolent man, and Jesus was commanded to journey to him to call him and the people of that city to turn back to God. He went until he drew near the city, with the disciples accompanying him, and he said to his companions: "Is there not a man among you who will set out to the city and proclaim in it, saying: 'Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger'?" A man of the disciples called Yaʿqūb stood up and said: "I will, O Spirit of God." He said: "Then go; but you will be the first to disown me." Another, called Tūṣār, stood up and said to him: "I will go with him." He said: "And you, with him." The two walked off, and Simon stood up and said: "O Spirit of God, let me be the third of them, and permit me to speak against you if I am compelled to that." He said: "Yes." They set off, until, when they were near the city, Simon said to the two of them: "Enter the city and deliver what you have been commanded, and I will stay in my place; if you are put to trial, I will devise a stratagem for you." The two went on until they entered the city, where the people were talking of the affair of Jesus, saying the vilest things about him and about his mother. One of them, the first, called out: "Hear ye! Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger." They leapt upon the two of them: "Who is it that says that Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger?" The one who had called out disowned it and said: "I said nothing." Then the other said: "You did say it, and I say it: Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger, and His word which He cast unto Mary, and a spirit from Him; so believe in him, O company of the Children of Israel, it is better for you." They took him off to their king, who was a tyrannical and oppressive man, and he said to him: "Woe to you, what are you saying?" He said: "I say: Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger, and His word which He cast unto Mary, and a spirit from Him." He said: "You lie." And they slandered Jesus and his mother with calumny. Then he said to him: "Woe to you, disown Jesus and say about him what we say." He said: "I will not do it." He said: "If you do not, I will cut off your hands and your feet and put out your eyes with nails." He said: "Do with us what you are going to do." So he did that to him and threw him on a rubbish heap in the middle of their city. Then the king was minded to cut out his tongue, when Simon came in, the people having gathered, and said to them: "What has this poor wretch said?" They said: "He claims that Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger." Simon said: "O king, will you permit me to go near to him and question him?" He said: "Yes." Simon said to him: "O afflicted one, what do you say?" He said: "I say: Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger." He said: "And what is his sign? Do you know him?" He said: "He heals the one born blind and the leper and the sick." He said: "The physicians do this; is there anything else?" He said: "Yes, he tells you what you eat and what you store away." He said: "The soothsayers know this; is there anything other than this?" He said: "Yes, he creates out of clay the likeness of a bird." He said: "This the sorcerers can do; he will have taken it from them." The king began to marvel at him and at his questioning. He said: "Is there anything other than this?" He said: "Yes, he gives life to the dead." He said: "O king, he has mentioned a mighty matter, and I do not think any creature has power over that except by the permission of God; and God would not bring that to pass at the hand of a lying sorcerer. If Jesus were not a messenger he would have no power over that, and God has not done that for anyone except for Abraham, when he asked Him: Show me how You give life to the dead (2:260). And who is like Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful!"

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Suddī, and Ibn ʿAsākir, by way of al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik and from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When God sent Jesus and commanded him to call to Him, the Children of Israel confronted him and drove him out. So he and his mother went out wandering in the land, and they lodged in a village with a man who gave them hospitality and treated them well. That city had a tyrannical king. One day that man came home grieving, and entered his house while Mary was with his wife. She said to her: "What is the matter with your husband? I see him grieving!" She said: "We have a king who imposes on each man among us a day on which he must feed him and his soldiers and give them wine to drink, and if he does not do so he punishes him; and his turn has come today, and we have not the means." She said: "Tell him not to worry, for I shall tell my son and he will pray for him, and he will be spared that." Mary spoke to Jesus about that, and Jesus said: "O mother, if I do it there will be evil in it." She said: "Do not mind that, for he has been good to us and honoured us." Jesus said: "Tell him: fill your cooking-pots and your jars with water." He filled them, and Jesus prayed to God, and what was in the pots turned into meat, broth and bread, and what was in the jars into wine the like of which the people had never seen. When the king came he ate of it, and when he drank the wine he asked: "Where did you get this wine?" He said: "It is from such-and-such a land." The king said: "But my wine is brought to me from that land, and it is not like this!" He said: "It is from another land." When he had confused the king, the king pressed him hard, and so he said: "I will tell you: I have with me a boy who never asks God for anything but He gives it to him, and he prayed to God and turned the water into wine." The king said to him, now he had had a son whom he wished to make his successor, who had died a few days before that, and who had been the dearest of creatures to him, he said: "A man who prayed to God and He turned the water into wine will surely be answered if he prays that my son be brought back to life." So he summoned Jesus and spoke with him, and asked him to pray to God to give life to his son. Jesus said: "Do not do it, for if he lives it will be an evil." The king said: "I do not care; shall I not see him? I do not care what happens." Jesus (peace be upon him) said: "If I bring him to life, will you leave me and my mother to go wherever we wish?" The king said: "Yes." So he prayed to God, and the boy lived. When the people of his kingdom saw that he had come to life, they called one another to arms and said: "This one has devoured us, until, when his death drew near, he wants to set his son over us as his successor, to devour us as his father devoured us!" So they fought one another, and Jesus and his mother went away, and a Jew accompanied the two of them. The Jew had two loaves and Jesus had one loaf. Jesus said to him: "Will you share with me?" The Jew said: "Yes." But when he saw that Jesus (peace be upon him) had only one loaf, he regretted it. When the two slept, the Jew set about trying to eat the loaf; he would eat a mouthful and Jesus would say to him: "What are you doing?" and he would say: "Nothing," until he had finished the loaf. When morning came, Jesus said to him: "Bring out your food." He brought one loaf, and Jesus said to him: "Where is the other loaf?" He said: "I had only one." He let it pass. They set off and passed by a shepherd of sheep, and Jesus called out: "O owner of the sheep, give us a sheep from your flock to slaughter." He said: "Yes," and gave him a sheep, which he slaughtered and roasted. Then he said to the Jew: "Eat, and do not break a bone." They ate, and when they were full Jesus threw the bones into the skin, then struck it with his staff and said: "Rise, by the permission of God." The sheep stood up, bleating. He said: "O owner of the sheep, take your sheep." The shepherd said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Jesus son of Mary." He said: "You are the sorcerer?" and fled from him. Jesus said to the Jew: "By Him who gave life to this sheep after we had eaten it, how many loaves did you have?" He swore that he had had only one loaf. Then he passed by an owner of cattle and said: "O owner of the cattle, give us a calf from these cattle of yours to slaughter." He gave it to him, and he slaughtered it and roasted it while the owner of the cattle looked on. Jesus said to him: "Eat, and do not break a bone." When they had finished, he threw the bones into the skin, then struck it with his staff and said: "Rise, by the permission of God." It rose up, lowing. He said: "O owner of the cattle, take your calf." He said: "And who are you?" He said: "I am Jesus." He said: "You are Jesus the sorcerer?" and then fled from him. Jesus said to the Jew: "By Him who gave life to this sheep after we had eaten it, and the calf after we had eaten it, how many loaves did you have?" He swore by that that he had had only one loaf. The two went on until they stopped at a village; the Jew lodged in the upper part of it and Jesus in the lower part. The Jew took a staff like the staff of Jesus and said: "Now I will give life to the dead." The king of that village was ill, gravely ill, so the Jew went about calling: "Who is seeking a physician?" He was told of the king and his malady, and he said: "Bring me in to him and I will cure him; and if you see that he has died, I will bring him back to life." He was told: "The king's malady has baffled the physicians before you." He said: "Bring me in to him." So he was brought in to him, and he took hold of the king's leg and struck him with his staff until he died, and he kept striking him while he was dead, saying: "Rise, by the permission of God."

So they seized him to crucify him. That reached Jesus, and he came to him when he had already been hoisted onto the wooden beam, and said: "What do you say: if I bring your companion back to life for you, will you leave my companion to me?" They said: "Yes." So Jesus brought the king back to life, and he stood up and brought the Jew down. He said: "O Jesus, you are the man to whom I owe the greatest favour of all people; by God, I will never part from you." Jesus said: "I adjure you by Him who gave life to the sheep and the calf after we had eaten them both, and gave life to this man after he had died, and brought you down from the trunk after you had been hoisted onto it to be crucified: how many loaves did you have?" He swore by all of this that he had had only one loaf. The two went on and passed by three bricks, and Jesus prayed to God and He turned them into gold. He said: "O Jew, one brick is for me, one brick is for you, and one brick is for the one who ate the loaf." He said: "I ate the loaf."

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from Layth, who said: A man accompanied Jesus son of Mary. The two set off and came to the bank of a river, and sat down to eat the midday meal; they had three loaves with them. They ate the two loaves and one loaf remained. Jesus got up to go to the river to drink, then came back and did not find the loaf. He said to the man: "Who ate the loaf?" He said: "I do not know." He went on with him and saw a gazelle with two fawns. He called one of the two and it came to him; he slaughtered it and roasted it, and they ate. Then he said to the fawn: "Rise, by the permission of God," and it rose. He said to the man: "I ask you, by Him who showed you this sign, who took the loaf?" He said: "I do not know." Then they came to the sea, and Jesus took the man by the hand and walked upon the water. Then he said: "I adjure you, by Him who showed you this sign, who took the loaf?" He said: "I do not know." Then they came to a cave, and Jesus took earth and clay and said: "Be gold, by the permission of God," and it became gold. He divided it into three thirds and said: "A third is for you, a third is for me, and a third is for the one who took the loaf." He said: "I took it." He said: "Then all of it is yours." And Jesus parted from him. Two men came upon him and wanted to take it and kill him. He said: "It is between us in thirds; so send one of you to the village to buy us food." They sent one of them, and the one who was sent said: "Why should I share the money with these two? Rather, I will put poison in the food and kill them." And those two said: "Why should we give this one a third of the money? Rather, when he comes back we will kill him." When he came back to them they killed him, and the two ate the food and died. So that money remained in the cave, with those three lying dead beside it.

Aḥmad recorded in al-Zuhd, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: When Jesus son of Mary sent out his messengers to give life to the dead, he would say to them: "Say such-and-such, say such-and-such; and when you feel a shudder and a tear, then make the supplication at that moment."

Aḥmad recorded in al-Zuhd, from Thābit, who said: Jesus (peace be upon him) set out to visit a brother of his, and a person met him and said: "Your brother has died." So he turned back. The daughters of his brother heard that he had turned back from them, so they came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, your turning back from us is harder upon us than the death of our father." He said: "Then go and show me his grave." They went until they showed him his grave. He said: He called out to him, and he came forth, white-haired. He said: "Are you not so-and-so?" He said: "Yes, indeed." He said: "Then what is this that I see upon you?" He said: "I heard your voice and thought it was the Cry."
### His words, Exalted: and I inform you (3:49), the verse.

Al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Mujāhid, concerning His words and I inform you of what you eat and what you store (3:49): He said: Of what food you ate last night, and what of it you hid away.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Jesus used to say to the boy in the school: "Your family have hidden away such-and-such for you." That is His words: and what you store (3:49).

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: Jesus son of Mary, while he was a boy, used to play with the children, and he would say to one of them: "Do you want me to tell you what your mother has hidden away for you?" He would say: "Yes." He would say: "She has hidden away such-and-such for you." The boy among them would go to his mother and say to her: "Feed me what you hid away for me." She would say: "And what have I hidden away for you?" He would say: "Such-and-such." She would say: "Who told you?" He would say: "Jesus son of Mary." So they said: "By God, if you leave these children with Jesus he will surely corrupt them." So they gathered them in a house and locked them in. Jesus went out seeking them and did not find them, until he heard their clamour in a house. He asked about them, saying: "O you people, it seems these are the children." They said: "No, these are only apes and swine." He said: "O God, make them apes and swine." And they became so.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, who said: and I inform you of what you eat (3:49): of the Table; and what you store (3:49): of it. A covenant had been taken from them concerning the Table, when it came down, that they should eat and not store away; but they stored away and acted treacherously, and so they were made into apes and swine.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd: and what you store (3:49), read with the doubled letter, by assimilation (idghām).{{fn:That is, taddakhirūn, the standard reading in which the dhāl of the root is assimilated into the dāl of the verbal form, as against the lighter reading tadhkharūn.}}
### His words, Exalted: and confirming what was before me (3:50), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Wahb, that Jesus was upon the law (sharīʿah) of Moses (peace be upon them both); he used to keep the Sabbath and to face Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) in prayer, and he said to the Children of Israel: "I have not called you to go against a single letter of what is in the Torah, except to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you, and to lift from you some of the burdens."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Rabīʿ, concerning His words and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you (3:50): He said: What Jesus brought was gentler than what Moses brought. In what Moses brought, the flesh of camels and the fat of the entrails (thurūb) had been forbidden to them, and He made these lawful for them by the tongue of Jesus; the fats had been forbidden to them, and they were made lawful for them in what Jesus brought; and likewise certain kinds of fish, and certain kinds of birds, those which have no spur (ṣīṣiyah), and other things which He had forbidden them and in which He had been severe upon them; so Jesus came to them with the lightening of that in the Gospel.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Qatādah, the like of it.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Mujāhid, concerning His words and I have come to you with a sign from your Lord (3:50): He said: All the things that Jesus made clear to them, and what his Lord gave him.
### His words, Exalted: Then when Jesus perceived (3:52), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words Then when Jesus perceived unbelief from them (3:52): He said: They disbelieved and wanted to kill him; that is when he sought the help of his people, and that is when He says: so a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved (61:14).
Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Mujāhid: Who are my helpers unto God? (3:52). He said: Who will follow me unto God?
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Suddī: Who are my helpers unto God? (3:52). He says: with God.
### His words, Exalted: The disciples said (3:52), the verse.

Al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: They were called the disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) only because of the whiteness of their garments; they were fishermen.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Abū Arṭāh, who said: The disciples were the washermen who whiten (yuḥawwirūn) garments, that is, wash them.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The disciples were the washermen; in Nabataean it is hawwārī, and in Arabic, al-muḥawwar (the whitened).
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The disciples were fullers; Jesus passed by them and they believed in him and followed him.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Qatādah, who said: The disciples are those who are fit for succession.{{fn:That is, fit to succeed the prophets as their deputies (khilāfah).}}
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The disciples are the chosen ones (aṣfiyāʾ) of the prophets.
Ibn Mardawayh recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The disciples are the chosen ones of the prophets.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Qatādah, who said: The ḥawārī is the minister (wazīr).
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, who said: The ḥawārī is the helper.

Al-Bukhārī, al-Tirmidhī and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "Every prophet has a disciple (ḥawārī), and my disciple is al-Zubayr."

Ibn Abī Dāwūd recorded in al-Maṣāḥif, from Asīd ibn Yazīd, who said: "And bear witness that we are Muslims" (wa-shhad bi-annanā muslimūn) (3:52) is in the codex (muṣḥaf) of ʿUthmān in three letters.{{fn:That is, the particle after bi- is written in ʿUthmān's codex in the shorter form of three letters, annā, rather than the fuller annanā.}}
### His words, Exalted: Our Lord, we believe (3:53), the verse.

Al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words so write us down among the witnesses (3:53): He said: With Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and his community; for they bore witness for him that he had conveyed the message, and they bore witness for the messengers that they had conveyed it.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded, by way of al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: so write us down among the witnesses (3:53). He said: With the Companions of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

Ibn Mardawayh recorded, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say when he had finished his prayer: "O God, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, for those who ask of You have a right upon You, that whatever servant or handmaid among the people of the land and the sea whose call You have accepted and whose supplication You have answered, You make us partners in the good of what they ask of You, and that You grant well-being to us and to them, and accept from us and from them, and pardon us and them; for we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger, so write us down among the witnesses." And he used to say: "No one of His creatures speaks these words but that God makes him a partner in the supplication of the people of their land and the people of their sea, so that it encompasses them all while he remains in his place."

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Suddī, who said: The Children of Israel besieged Jesus and nineteen men of the disciples in a house. Jesus said to his companions: "Who will take on my likeness and be killed, and Paradise shall be his?" One of them took it on, and Jesus was taken up to heaven. That is His words: And they schemed, and God schemed; and God is the best of schemers (3:54).
### His words, Exalted: When God said: O Jesus (3:55), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words I am taking you (3:55) (mutawaffīka): He says: I am causing you to die.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan, who said: taking you (3:55): from the earth.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by another route, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words I am taking you (3:55): meaning the taking of sleep; God raised him in his sleep. Al-Ḥasan said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the Jews: "Jesus has not died, and he is returning to you before the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Qatādah: I am taking you and raising you to Myself (3:55). He said: This is of the kind in which what comes first is put later and what comes later is put first (al-muqaddam wa-l-muʾakhkhar), that is: raising you to Myself and taking you.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Maṭar al-Warrāq, concerning the verse: He said: Taking you from this world, and it is not the taking of death.

Ibn Jarīr recorded, with a sound chain, from Kaʿb, who said: When Jesus saw the fewness of those who followed him and the multitude of those who denied him, he complained of that to God, and God revealed to him: I am taking you and raising you to Myself (3:55), and one whom I have raised to Myself is not dead; and I shall send you against the one-eyed Dajjāl{{fn:The Dajjāl is the false messiah, or Antichrist, whom Muslim tradition expects at the end of time.}} and you will kill him; then after that you will live twenty-four years; then I shall cause you to die the death of the living. Kaʿb said: And that is the confirmation of the ḥadīth of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) where he said: "How can a community perish of which I am at the beginning and Jesus at the end?"

Isḥāq ibn Bishr and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from al-Ḥasan, who said: There was no prophet in whose time wonders were more numerous than Jesus, until God raised him. Among the causes of his being raised was that a tyrannical king called Dāwūd ibn Nūdhā, who was the king of the Children of Israel, was the one who sent in search of him to kill him. God had sent down the Gospel to him when he was thirteen years old, and he was raised when he was thirty-four years from his birth. So God revealed to him: I am taking you and raising you to Myself and purifying you from those who disbelieve (3:55), meaning: and delivering you from the Jews, so that they shall not be able to kill you.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by another route, from al-Ḥasan, concerning the verse: He said: God raised him to Himself, and he is with Him in heaven.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Wahb, who said: God made Jesus son of Mary die for three hours of the day, until He raised him to Himself.
Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from Wahb, who said: God made him die for three days, then raised him up and lifted him.

Al-Ḥākim recorded, from Wahb, that God made Jesus die for seven hours, then brought him to life; and that Mary conceived him when she was thirteen years old; and that he was raised at the age of thirty-three; and that his mother remained six years after he was raised.

Isḥāq ibn Bishr and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, by way of Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words I am taking you and raising you (3:55): meaning raising you, then taking you at the end of time.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning the verse: He said: His raising him is His taking him.

Al-Ḥākim recorded, from al-Ḥurayth ibn Makhashsh, that ʿAlī was killed on the morning of the twenty-first of Ramaḍān, "and I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī saying: He was killed on the night the Qurʾān was sent down, the night Jesus was taken up by night, and the night Moses was taken."
Ibn Saʿd, Aḥmad in al-Zuhd and al-Ḥākim recorded, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Jesus was raised at the age of thirty-three years, and Muʿādh died at that same age.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words and purifying you from those who disbelieve (3:55): He said: He purified him from the Jews, the Christians and the Magians, and from the unbelievers of his people.
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: and purifying you from those who disbelieve (3:55). He said: When they intended against you what they intended.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Qatādah, concerning His words and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection (3:55): He said: They are the people of Islam, who followed him upon his natural disposition (fiṭrah), his religion and his way; they shall not cease to prevail over those who oppose them until the Day of Resurrection.
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning the verse: He said: Giving victory to those who follow you in Islam over those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "A party of my community shall not cease to prevail, not caring who opposes them, until the command of God comes." Al-Nuʿmān said: So whoever says that I am attributing to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) what he did not say, the confirmation of this is in the Book of God, Exalted; God, Exalted, said: and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection (3:55), the verse.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan: and placing those who follow you (3:55). He said: They are the Muslims, and we are of them, and we are above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "A band of my community shall never cease to fight for the truth, prevailing over the people, until the command of God comes while they are upon that." Then he drew upon this verse: O Jesus, I am taking you and raising you to Myself and purifying you from those who disbelieve and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection (3:55).

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Ibn Zayd, concerning the verse: He said: The Christians are above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection; there is no land in which there is any of the Christians but that they are above the Jews, in east or west; the Jews are humbled in all lands.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded, from al-Ḥasan, concerning the verse: He said: Jesus is raised up with God, then he will descend before the Day of Resurrection; and whoever believes in Jesus and in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and is upon their religion, they shall not cease to prevail over those who part from them until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Jarīr recorded, by way of ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds (3:57): He says: who perform My obligations; He will pay them their rewards in full (3:57): He says: He will give them the recompense of their righteous deeds complete, nothing of it being withheld from them, nor will they diminish it.
### His words, Exalted: This We recite to you (3:58), the verse.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The two monks of Najrān came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and one of them said: "Who is the father of Jesus?" The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would not hasten until he had consulted his Lord, and there came down to him: This We recite to you of the signs and the wise Remembrance (3:58), up to His words: of the doubters (3:60).
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning His words and the wise Remembrance (3:58): He said: The Qurʾān.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from ʿAlī: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "There will be trials (fitan)." I said: "What is the way out of them?" He said: "The Book of God; it is the wise Remembrance and the straight path."
His words, Exalted: Surely the likeness of Jesus (3:59), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that a group of the people of Najrān{{fn:a Christian town and district in the south of Arabia, whose delegation came to the Prophet in Medina}} came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and among them were al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib{{fn:the two leading men of the Christian delegation of Najrān: al-Sayyid was their chief and al-ʿĀqib his deputy and the holder of their counsel}}. They said to him: “What is it with you, that you speak of our companion?” He said: “Who is he?” They said: “Jesus; you claim that he is the servant of God!” He said: “Indeed, he is the servant of God.” They said: “Have you ever seen the like of Jesus, or been told of one?” Then they went out from his presence, and Gabriel came to him and said: Say to them when they come to you: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), to the end of the verse.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the two lords of the people of Najrān and their two bishops, al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib, met the Prophet of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and asked him about Jesus. They said: “Every son of Adam has a father; so what is the case of Jesus, who has no father?” So God sent down concerning him this verse: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God (3:59), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr recorded from al-Suddī, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent and the people of Najrān heard of him, four men from among the best of them came to him, among them al-ʿĀqib, al-Sayyid, Māsarjis and Mārbaḥr. They asked him what he said about Jesus. He said: “He is the servant of God, and His spirit, and His word.” They said: “No; rather he is God, who came down from His kingdom and entered into the womb of Mary, then came forth from her, and so showed us His power and His command. Have you ever seen a human being created without a father?” So God sent down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿIkrimah concerning His words: Surely the likeness of Jesus (3:59), the verse. He said: It was sent down concerning al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid of the people of Najrān.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It has reached us that the delegation of the Christians of Najrān came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), among them al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib, who at that time were the two lords of the people of Najrān. They said: “O Muḥammad, why do you revile our companion?” He said: “Who is your companion?” They said: “Jesus son of Mary; you claim that he is a servant.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Indeed, he is the servant of God and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him.” They grew angry and said: “If you are truthful, then show us a servant who gives life to the dead, heals the blind from birth, and creates from clay the likeness of a bird and breathes into it”, the verse, “No, rather he is God.” He kept silent until Gabriel came to him and said: “O Muḥammad, They have certainly disbelieved who say that God is the Messiah, son of Mary (5:17), the verse.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “O Gabriel, they asked me to tell them of the likeness of Jesus.” Gabriel said: The likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him “Be”, and he was.
When morning came they returned, and he recited the verses to them.

Ibn Saʿd and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded from al-Azraq ibn Qays, who said: The bishop of Najrān and al-ʿĀqib came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he offered Islam to them. They said: “We were already Muslims before you.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “You both lie. Three things keep you from Islam: your saying that God has taken a son, your prostration to the cross, and your eating the flesh of swine.” They said: “Then who is the father of Jesus?” He did not know what to say, and so God sent down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), up to His words the corrupters (3:63). When these verses came down, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called the two of them to mutual imprecation (mulāʿanah){{fn:the solemn procedure of 3:61 in which each party calls down the curse of God upon whichever of them is lying; also called mubāhalah}}, and they said: “If he is a prophet, it is not fitting for us to imprecate against him.” So they refused, and said: “Do you offer anything other than this?” He said: “Islam, or the poll-tax (jizyah), or war.” So they agreed to the poll-tax.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from Qatādah: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters (3:60), meaning: do not be in doubt concerning Jesus, that he is as the likeness of Adam, the servant of God, His messenger and His word.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The delegation of Najrān came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “Tell us about Jesus son of Mary.” He said: “The messenger of God and His word which He cast to Mary.” They said: “Jesus ought to be above this.” So God sent down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), the verse. They said: “Jesus ought not to be like Adam.” So God sent down: So whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you (3:61), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Would that there were a veil between me and the people of Najrān, so that I should not see them and they should not see me”, because of the severity with which they used to dispute with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

Al-Bayhaqī recorded in al-Dalāʾil, by way of Salamah ibn ʿAbd Yashūʿ, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) wrote to the people of Najrān, before Ṭā Sīn Sulaymān{{fn:that is, Sūrat al-Naml (27), which opens with the letters Ṭā Sīn and contains Solomon's letter beginning “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful” (27:30); before it was revealed the Prophet's letters opened with the older formula “In the name of the God of…” or “In Your name, O God”}} was sent down to him: “In the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), to the bishop of Najrān and the people of Najrān. If you submit, then I praise to you God, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. To proceed: I call you to the worship of God rather than the worship of servants, and I call you to the guardianship of God rather than the guardianship of servants. If you refuse, then the poll-tax; and if you refuse that, then I have given you notice of war. And peace.” When the bishop read the letter he was appalled by it and seized with a great dread, and he sent for a man of the people of Najrān called Shuraḥbīl ibn Wadāʿah and handed him the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). He read it, and the bishop said to him: “What is your view?” Shuraḥbīl said: “You know what God promised Abraham concerning prophethood among the descendants of Ishmael; so what is to guarantee that this is not that man? I have no opinion to give on prophethood; were it a matter of worldly affairs I would counsel you in it and strive on your behalf.” The bishop then sent for one man after another of the people of Najrān, and every one of them said the same as Shuraḥbīl had said. So their opinion was agreed that they should send Shuraḥbīl ibn Wadāʿah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shuraḥbīl and Jabbār ibn Fayḍ, to bring them back news of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). The delegation set out until they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him); he questioned them and they questioned him, and the questioning went on between him and them until they said to him: “What do you say about Jesus son of Mary?” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “I have nothing on him this day of mine; so stay until I inform you of what is told me concerning Jesus tomorrow morning.” Then God sent down this verse: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), up to His words: and invoke the curse of God upon the liars (3:61). They refused to acknowledge that, and when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) rose the next morning, after he had told them the news, he came forward wrapping al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn in a cloak of his, with Fāṭimah walking behind his back, for the mutual imprecation; and he had at that time a number of wives. Shuraḥbīl said to his two companions: “I see a matter coming upon us. If this man is a prophet sent by God and we imprecate against him, there will not remain on the face of the earth of us a hair or a nail but it will perish.” They said to him: “What is your view?” He said: “My view is that I should let him be the judge over us, for I see a man who will never judge unjustly.” They said to him: “It is yours to decide.” Shuraḥbīl went to meet the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “I have seen something better than imprecating against you.” He said: “And what is it?” He said: “Your judgement, this day until nightfall and your night until the morning; whatever you judge concerning us is binding.” So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) went back and did not imprecate against them, and made peace with them on terms of the poll-tax.

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Ḥudhayfah that al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he wished to imprecate against them, but one of them said to his companion: “Do not imprecate against him, for by God, if he is a prophet and he imprecates against us, neither we nor our posterity after us will ever prosper.” So they said to him: “We will give you what you have asked; so send with us a trustworthy man.” He said: “Rise, O Abū ʿUbaydah.” And when he stood up he said: “This is the trustee of this community.”

Al-Ḥākim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Jābir, who said: Al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he called them to Islam. They said: “We have submitted, O Muḥammad.”

He said: “You both lie. If you wish, I shall tell you what keeps you from Islam.” They said: “Go on, then.” He said: “Love of the cross, drinking of wine, and eating the flesh of swine.” Jābir said: Then he called them to mutual imprecation, and they made an appointment with him for the morrow. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) went out in the morning and took ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn by the hand, then sent for the two of them; but they refused to answer him and yielded to him. He said: “By Him who sent me with the truth, had they done it, the valley would have rained fire upon them.” Jābir said: Concerning them was sent down: Come, let us call our sons and your sons (3:61), the verse. Jābir said: and ourselves and yourselves (3:61): the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and ʿAlī; our sons (3:61): al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn; and our women (3:61): Fāṭimah.

Al-Ḥākim, who declared it sound, recorded from Jābir that the delegation of Najrān came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “What do you say about Jesus?” He said: “He is the spirit of God and His word, and the servant of God and His messenger.” They said to him: “Are you willing that we should imprecate with you that it is not so?” He said: “Is that more pleasing to you?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Then whenever you wish.” He came and gathered his offspring, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and their chief said: “Do not imprecate against this man, for by God, if you imprecate against him, one of the two parties will surely be swallowed up by the earth.” So they came and said: “O Abū al-Qāsim, it was only our foolish ones who wished to imprecate against you, and we would like you to excuse us.” He said: “I have excused you.” Then he said: “The punishment had overshadowed Najrān.”

Abū Nuʿaym recorded in al-Dalāʾil, by way of al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the delegation of Najrān, of the Christians, came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), fourteen men of their nobles, among them al-Sayyid, who was the great one among them, and al-ʿĀqib, who was the one next after him and the holder of their counsel. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the two of them: “Submit.” They said: “We have submitted.” He said: “You have not submitted.” They said: “Yes indeed, we submitted before you.” He said: “You both lie. Three things in you keep you from Islam: your worship of the cross, your eating of swine, and your claim that God has a son.” And there came down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust (3:59), the verse. When he recited it to them they said: “We do not recognise what you say.” And there came down: So whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you (3:61). He says: whoever argues with you about the matter of Jesus after there has come to you of the knowledge (3:61), of the Qurʾān, then say: Come (3:61), up to His words: then let us earnestly pray (3:61). He says: let us strive in supplication that what Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) has brought is the truth and that what they say is falsehood. He said to them: “God has commanded me, if you do not accept this, to engage you in mutual imprecation (mubāhalah).” They said: “O Abū al-Qāsim, rather let us go back and consider our affair, then we will come to you.” They withdrew with one another and spoke frankly among themselves. Al-Sayyid said to al-ʿĀqib: “By God, you know that the man is a prophet sent by God, and if you imprecate against him it will mean your extirpation; never did a people imprecate against a prophet and their elder survive or their young one grow up. So if you will not follow him and insist only on clinging to your religion, then make a truce with him and return to your country.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had gone out with ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn and Fāṭimah with him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “When I pray, say Amen.” But they refused to imprecate against him and made peace with him on terms of the poll-tax.

Abū Nuʿaym recorded in al-Dalāʾil, by way of ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that eight of the bishops of the Arabs, of the people of Najrān, came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), among them al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid. So God sent down: then say: Come, let us call our sons (3:61), up to His words: then let us earnestly pray (3:61). He means: let us call upon God to lay the curse upon the liar. They said: “Grant us a delay of three days.” So they went to Banū Qurayẓah, al-Naḍīr and Banū Qaynuqāʿ{{fn:the three Jewish tribes of Medina}} and consulted them, and these counselled them to make peace with him and not to imprecate against him, for he was the prophet whom we find in the Torah. So they made peace with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) on terms of a thousand garments in Ṣafar and a thousand in Rajab, and dirhams.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Qatādah: So whoever disputes with you concerning him (3:61): concerning Jesus; then say: Come, let us call our sons (3:61), the verse. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) summoned the delegation of Najrān to this, and they are the ones who had disputed with him concerning Jesus; but they drew back and refused. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Punishment had indeed come down upon the people of Najrān; had they done it, they would have been extirpated from the face of the earth.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym recorded from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The people of Najrān were the most extreme of the Christians in what they said about Jesus son of Mary, and they used to argue with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about him. So God sent down these verses in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God (3:59), up to His words: and invoke the curse of God upon the liars (3:61). He was commanded to engage them in mutual imprecation, and they made an appointment with him for the morrow. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) went out in the morning with al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn and Fāṭimah with him; but they refused to imprecate against him and made peace with him on terms of the poll-tax. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The bearer of tidings came to me with the destruction of the people of Najrān, even to the birds upon the trees, had they gone through with the mutual imprecation.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Bukhārī, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Had the people of Najrān engaged in mutual imprecation with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), they would have returned to find neither family nor property.

Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan recorded from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who said: When this verse was sent down: then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons (3:61), the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, and said: “O God, these are my family.”

Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿAlbāʾ ibn Aḥmar al-Yashkurī, who said: When this verse was sent down: then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons (3:61), the verse, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent for ʿAlī, Fāṭimah and their two sons al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and summoned the Jews to imprecate against them. A young man of the Jews said: “Woe to you! Is it not within your recent memory, as of yesterday, that your brethren were transformed into apes and swine? Do not imprecate.” So they desisted.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, concerning this verse: Come, let us call our sons (3:61), the verse. He said: He brought Abū Bakr and his son, ʿUmar and his son, ʿUthmān and his son, and ʿAlī and his son.
Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn ʿAbbās: then let us earnestly pray (3:61): let us strive in supplication.

Al-Ḥākim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “This is sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ),” pointing with the finger next to the thumb; “and this is supplication (duʿāʾ),” and he raised his hands level with his shoulders; “and this is earnest entreaty (ibtihāl),” and he raised his hands stretched out high.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās: Surely this is the true narrative (3:62). He says: surely this which We have said concerning Jesus is the truth.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded from Qays ibn Saʿd, who said: There was something between Ibn ʿAbbās and another man, and he recited this verse: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us earnestly pray (3:61), and he raised his hands and faced the Corner{{fn:the corner of the Kaʿbah in which the Black Stone is set}}: and invoke the curse of God upon the liars (3:61).
His words, Exalted: Say: O People of the Book, come (3:64), the verse.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite in the two rakʿahs of dawn, in the first of them: Say: We believe in God and what has been sent down to us (2:136), the verse; and in the second: Come to a word common between us and you (3:64).

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Abū Sufyān related to me that Heraclius called for the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and read it, and in it was: “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: I call you with the summons of Islam. Submit, and you will be safe; submit, and God will give you your reward twice over. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the arīsiyyīn{{fn:the peasants or subject tillers of the land under Byzantine rule; the sin of their remaining outside Islam would fall upon Heraclius if he turned them away from it}}. O People of the Book, come to a word common between us and you: that we worship none but God, and that we associate nothing with Him (3:64),” up to His words: bear witness that we are Muslims (3:64).

Al-Ṭabarānī recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās that the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to the unbelievers was: Come to a word common between us and you (3:64), to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: Come to a word (3:64), the verse. He said: It has reached me that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the Jews of the people of Medina to that, but they refused him; so he fought them until they agreed to the poll-tax (jizyah).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the Jews of the people of Medina to the common word; they are the ones who disputed concerning Abraham and claimed that he died a Jew, so God gave them the lie and disowned them from him, saying: O People of the Book, why do you dispute concerning Abraham (3:65), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr recorded from al-Rabīʿ, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the Jews to the common word.

He recorded from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr concerning His words: Say: O People of the Book, come (3:64), the verse. He said: So he called them to a fair settlement and cut off the argument from them, meaning the delegation of Najrān.

He recorded from al-Suddī, who said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called them, meaning the delegation of the Christians of Najrān, and said: O People of the Book, come to a common word (3:64), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Qatādah: Come to a word common (3:64). He said: just.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded the like of it from al-Rabīʿ.

Al-Ṭastī recorded in his Masāʾil{{fn:the “Questions of Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq”, a collection of lexical questions put to Ibn ʿAbbās, each answered with a verse of Arabic poetry}} from Ibn ʿAbbās that Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq asked him about His words: common between us and you (3:64). He said: just. He said: And do the Arabs know that? He said: Yes; have you not heard the words of the poet:
> We met and settled our account on even terms (sawāʾ), but he was dragged from one state to another.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, who said: The common word is: there is no god but God.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Mujāhid: Come to a word common (3:64). He said: there is no god but God.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: and that none of us take others as lords apart from God (3:64). He said: that none of us obey another in disobedience to God.
