It was said to their kings: We find nothing harsher than the abuse these people heap upon us, for they recite: And whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, they are the disbelievers (5:44), And whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, they are the wrongdoers (5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, they are the sinners (5:47), together with the way they fault our deeds in their recitation. So summon them, and let them recite as we recite and believe as we believe. So he summoned them and gathered them, and offered them death, or else that they abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel except for what they had altered of it. They said: What do you want with that? Leave us be. One party of them said: Build us a pillar, then raise us up onto it, then give us something by which we may hoist up our food and drink, and we shall not come back to you. Another party said: Leave us to wander in the land and roam, and to eat of what the wild beasts eat and drink as they drink; and if you get hold of us in your land, kill us. Another party said: Build us houses in the wastelands, and we shall dig wells and cultivate vegetables, and we shall not come back to you nor pass by you. And there was no tribe but had a close kinsman among them. So they did that, and God sent down: and monasticism, which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them, only seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with the observance due to it (57:27). He said: And the others (those of the people of polytheism who took up devotions, after those of the former had passed away who passed away) said: We shall worship as so-and-so worshipped, and wander as so-and-so wandered, and take houses as so-and-so took them; yet they were upon their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those whom they imitated. When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent and only a few of them remained, the man of the cell came down from his cell, the wanderer came from his wandering, and the man of the monastery from his monastery, and they believed in him and affirmed him. So God Exalted said: O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you two portions of His mercy (57:28): two rewards, for their faith in Jesus, their wearying of themselves, and the Torah and the Gospel, and for their faith in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and their affirmation of him; and He will make for you a light by which you walk (57:28): the Qurʾān and their following the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

Abū Dāwūd, Abū Yaʿlā and al-Ḍiyāʾ reported from Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not be severe upon yourselves lest severity be imposed upon you; for a people were severe upon themselves and severity was imposed upon them, and those are their remnants in the cells and the monasteries: and monasticism, which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them (57:27)."

al-Ṭabarānī and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān reported from Sahl ibn Abī Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not be severe upon yourselves, for those who were before you perished only through their severity upon themselves; and you will find their remnants in the cells and the monasteries."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Naṣr reported from Abū Umāmah, who said: "God prescribed for you the fast of the month of Ramaḍān, but He did not prescribe for you its night prayer; the night prayer is only something you innovated, so persevere in it and do not abandon it; for some people of the Children of Israel innovated an innovation, and God faulted them for abandoning it," and he recited this verse: and monasticism, which they innovated (57:27), the verse.

Aḥmad, al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī, Abū Yaʿlā and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān reported from Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Every community has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this community is striving (jihād) in the way of God."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Qatādah concerning His words: and monasticism, which they innovated (57:27): he said: It was mentioned to us that they renounced women and took to cells.
### His words, Exalted: And when Jesus son of Mary said (61:6), the verse.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "I was the servant of God in the Mother of the Book, and the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still lying in his clay; and I shall tell you the interpretation of that: the supplication of my father Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus to his people, and the vision of my mother, who saw that a light came forth from her by which the palaces of Syria were lit up."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abū Mūsā, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded us to set out with Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib to the land of the Negus. When we came before the Negus he said: What prevents you from prostrating to me? I said: We prostrate to none but God. He said: And how is that? I said: God has sent among us His Messenger, and he is the Messenger of whom Jesus son of Mary gave glad tidings: a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad (61:6); and he has commanded us to worship God and not to associate anything with Him.

Mālik, al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Dārimī, al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī reported from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "I have names: I am Muḥammad, and I am Aḥmad, and I am al-Ḥāshir (the Gatherer), at whose feet mankind will be gathered, and I am al-Māḥī (the Effacer), by whom God effaces disbelief, and I am al-ʿĀqib (the Last)", and al-ʿĀqib is the one after whom there is no prophet.

al-Ṭayālisī and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "I am Muḥammad, and Aḥmad, and al-Ḥāshir, and the Prophet of Repentance, and the Prophet of the Fierce Battle (al-malḥamah)."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "I have been given what none of the prophets of God was given." We said: O Messenger of God, what is it? He said: "I have been aided with terror, I have been given the keys of the earth, I have been named Aḥmad, the soil of the earth has been made a means of purification for me, and my community has been made the best of communities."
### His words, Exalted: But when he came to them with the clear proofs (61:6), the verses.

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: But when he came to them with the clear proofs (61:6): he said: Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him); and concerning His words: They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths (61:8): he said: with their tongues.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported from Masrūq that he used to recite the one in al-Māʾidah, the one in al-Ṣaff and the one in Yūnus as sāḥir ("a sorcerer").{{fn:That is, he read "this is a manifest sorcerer" (hādhā sāḥirun mubīn) in place of "this is manifest sorcery" (hādhā siḥrun mubīn) at 5:110, 61:6 and 10:76.}}

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported from ʿĀṣim that he recited this is manifest sorcery (61:6) without an alif, and recited wa-llāhu mutimmun nūrahu (and God is the perfecter of His light, 61:8), putting tanwīn on mutimm and the accusative on nūrahu.
